vett-chat.vettPath.markdownDescription:
Absolute path to the `vett` binary. Leave empty to auto-detect in `~/.dotnet/tools/`, `~/go/bin/`, then `$PATH`. Set this only if `vett` lives somewhere unusual (custom build, mounted remote, etc.).

**Don't have vett yet?** See [VETT](https://github.com/msdickinson/vett#install): download `VettBench.*.nupkg` from its Releases, then `dotnet tool install --global --add-source <folder-with-the-nupkg> VettBench`.

vett-chat.profile.markdownDescription:
Name of the VETT profile to use for chat sessions. The profile is the **single source of truth** for endpoint, model, API key, system prompt, tools, and iteration budget. To change any of those, edit the profile YAML — not the extension settings.

Profile lookup order:
1. `<workspace>/profiles/<name>.yaml`
2. `~/.vett/profiles/<name>.yaml` (per-user override)
3. Bundled defaults shipped with vett

The default `coding` profile is chat-tuned (no auto-finish, conversational system prompt). Benchmark profiles like `openhands` will auto-terminate sessions and are not recommended for chat. Run `vett profiles` to see what's installed; use `Vett Chat: Pick Profile` from the Command Palette for an interactive picker.

vett-chat.chatSessionLogDir.markdownDescription:
Directory for JSONL chat session logs. Empty (default) writes to `~/.vett/chat-sessions/`. Override if your home directory is a slow network share or you want logs on a separate drive.

Logs are best-effort — write failures never break the chat path.

enumDescriptions: One line per tool call — status dot, tool name, one-line description, duration. Click to expand into the default view.
Header card with tool badge, human-readable description, and IN/OUT preview blocks. Click to expand the full data.
Header card plus full IN args and full OUT result inline at all times. Best for debugging.
vett-chat.toolCardDensity.markdownDescription:
How much detail to show per tool call in the Live chat view.

- `compact` — one line: `● Bash · List home dir ✓ 120ms`. Best for power users who scan dense logs.
- `default` — header card with truncated IN/OUT preview, click to expand. Good middle ground.
- `verbose` — full IN args and full OUT result inline. Best when actively debugging an agent run.

The Logs / Raw view modes are unaffected — this only changes the Live view's per-card rendering.

enumDescriptions: Compact event log: one line per event (timestamp · glyph · body). Dense, matches the Logs view's vocabulary, good for scanning a long sub-agent run.

Structured cards: sub-agent tool calls render with the same IN/OUT preview cards as the main chat; assistant text shows as message bubbles. Iteration / llm_request / llm_response boilerplate hidden. Better for following one task at a time.
vett-chat.dispatchViewStyle.markdownDescription:
How sub-agent dispatch cards render their event list when expanded.

- `log` (default): one line per event, like the Logs / Raw views. Compact and scannable.
- `structured`: sub-agent events render with the same `ToolCallCard` (IN/OUT preview, click-to-expand) the main chat uses, plus assistant-text message bubbles. Iteration markers + llm-request/response chatter are hidden.

Independent of `vett-chat.toolCardDensity` — that controls main-chat tool cards; this controls sub-agent dispatch cards.

vett-chat.contextWindowTokens.markdownDescription:
Total context window size, in tokens, for the active LLM. Drives the token-usage gauge in the status bar — `total / max` and the fill bar render against this number.

**Default 131072 (128k)** matches many current local models. Lower it to match smaller models (e.g. 8192 for a model with an 8k context) so the gauge fills meaningfully.

This is the model's hard ceiling, not where vett's middleware compacts the conversation. Compaction (via `MilestoneCheckpoint` / `LlmSummarizingCondenser`) runs earlier — much earlier than 128k — and is configured per-profile in YAML, independent of this setting.

vett-chat.useWorktree.markdownDescription:
Run each chat panel in an isolated git worktree at `~/.vett/worktrees/<workspace-hash>-<panel-id>/` instead of the user's working tree directly.

**Default: false.** Agent edits land directly in your workspace; you review them with your normal git workflow. Set to `true` when you want a hard isolation gate: vett edits the worktree only, your source tree stays untouched until you click **Apply changes to main tree** in the worktree-chip dropdown.

When the workspace is a git repo, isolation uses `git worktree add` on a hidden branch named `vett/wt-<panel-id>` — fast and cheap. Without `.git`, vett falls back to a recursive copy of the workspace, which can be very slow on large monorepos. If you turn this on against a non-git monorepo, expect a long first-message delay.

Per-panel and sticky for the panel's lifetime — toggling this setting affects new chat panels only. Existing panels keep their original mode.

vett-chat.smartActionsEnabled.markdownDescription:
Enable Vett's editor-surface AI buttons:

- **CodeLens** — `✨ Edit with Vett` floats above every function, method, class, interface, and constructor in your source files. Click it to open the inline-edit input box pre-targeted at that symbol.
- **QuickFix** — `Fix with Vett: <diagnostic>` appears in the lightbulb / Ctrl+. menu on every error and warning. Picking it runs an inline edit with the diagnostic message as the prefilled instruction.

Both surfaces ride on the same `vett edit` engine as `Cmd+I` / `Ctrl+I`, so the Diff → Apply / Cancel / Iterate flow is identical.

Disable to remove the visual noise without touching the inline-edit hotkey. Toggling refreshes the lens view live — no window reload required.

vett-chat.whisperEndpoint.markdownDescription:
URL of a Whisper-compatible HTTP endpoint for voice input. Used by the 🎤 Voice button in the chat input bar.

**Expected protocol** — OpenAI-style `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` accepting multipart/form-data with `file` + `model` + `response_format=json` fields. Returns `{ text: "..." }`. Compatible with whisper.cpp's HTTP server, Faster-Whisper-Server, and the official OpenAI API.

**Examples:**
- Self-hosted Whisper: `http://localhost:9000/v1/audio/transcriptions`
- OpenAI API: `https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions` (also set `vett-chat.whisperApiKey`, or export `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the shell that launches VS Code).

Leave empty to disable voice input.

vett-chat.whisperModel.markdownDescription: Model name passed in the Whisper request body. Most local servers ignore this field; the OpenAI API requires `whisper-1`. Faster-Whisper-Server uses tags like `Systran/faster-distil-whisper-large-v3`. Ignored when `vett-chat.whisperApiStyle` is `simple`.

enumDescriptions: Click 🎤 to start, click again to stop. Full audio is uploaded once on stop, transcript drops into the chat input. Works against any /transcribe endpoint.
Live captioning. Audio streams to the server over a WebSocket as you speak; partial transcripts append to the input field every ~1s. Requires the streaming-capable /ws/transcribe endpoint.
vett-chat.voiceMode.markdownDescription:
How the 🎤 voice button transcribes.

- `manual` (default): record then upload. One round-trip on stop, full transcript appears at once.
- `streaming`: WebSocket to `/ws/transcribe`, audio streams as you speak, partial transcripts live-update the chat input. Lower latency but requires a streaming server that exposes `/ws/transcribe`.

The streaming mode derives its WebSocket URL from `vett-chat.whisperEndpoint`: it strips a trailing `/transcribe` (or `/v1/audio/transcriptions`) and appends `/ws/transcribe`, then swaps `http` for `ws` (`https` for `wss`).

enumDescriptions: OpenAI-compatible — POST multipart with `file` + `model` + `response_format=json` to e.g. `/v1/audio/transcriptions`. Works with whisper.cpp's HTTP server, Faster-Whisper-Server, and OpenAI's hosted API.
Simple shape — POST multipart with a single `audio` form field to e.g. `/transcribe`. Matches the lightweight FastAPI Whisper wrappers (one binary file in, `{text: "..."}` out).
vett-chat.whisperApiStyle.markdownDescription:
Wire format vett-chat uses to talk to your STT server.

- `openai` (default): Multipart fields `file` + `model` + `response_format=json`. Endpoint typically ends with `/v1/audio/transcriptions`.
- `simple`: Single multipart field `audio`. Endpoint typically ends with `/transcribe`. Matches the lightweight FastAPI Whisper wrappers some self-hosted STT servers expose.

The response shape (`{text: "..."}`) is the same for both.

vett-chat.whisperApiKey.markdownDescription:
Bearer-auth API key for the Whisper endpoint. Local servers (whisper.cpp, faster-whisper) typically don't need this — leave empty.

For OpenAI's hosted Whisper (`https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions`) this key authenticates the request. If empty, voice input falls back to the `OPENAI_API_KEY` environment variable. Stored in your settings.json as plain text — only set this if you're comfortable with that trade-off.

vett-chat.ffmpegPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the `ffmpeg` binary, used for mic capture during voice input. Leave empty to use whatever's on `$PATH`. Set this only if `ffmpeg` isn't on your PATH or you want to pin a specific build.

vett-chat.voiceInputDevice.markdownDescription:
Override the input device name passed to ffmpeg.

- **Windows (DirectShow):** the audio device name shown by `ffmpeg -list_devices true -f dshow -i dummy`. Default: `default`.
- **macOS (AVFoundation):** index like `:0`, `:1`, `:2` from `ffmpeg -f avfoundation -list_devices true -i ""`. Default: `:0`.
- **Linux (PulseAudio):** source name from `pactl list short sources`. Default: `default`.

Leave empty to use the platform default.
